notes.decision: Tentatively translated 'Of the Teacher' on the assumption this is a variant or reduced form of the standard Kephalaia running header ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲁⲍ. The form ⲙ̄ⲧⲉⲁϩ is unusual; could alternatively be a specific section/chapter title. The decorative brackets [> ·] [· <] confirm its function as a running header.
Read as ⲛ̄-ⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'in the midst' (Lyc spelling with ⲓ̈ⲙ- for ⲛ̄ⲙ̄- and ⲙⲉⲧⲉ for ⲙⲏⲧⲉ). Mid-clause from preceding page; precise sense uncertain.
Translated 'way/road' from Coptic ⲡⲱⲧ 'race, course, road.' Could alternatively be Greek loan πύλη 'gate' with metathesis. Either fits 'drew them into the X of the city.'

Translated 'his heart.' ⲡⲉϩ- = Lyc 'his' + ⲧⲏⲩ likely for ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' (with metathesis or scribal variation), since 'fear in his X' demands a heart/breast term. Alternative: literal 'his wind/breath' (= ⲡⲧⲏⲩ) used idiomatically for courage/spirit.

Translated 'his other kingship' literally. ⲧⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲕⲉ- 'other' + ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲣⲟ 'kingship.' Sense in narrative obscure — possibly the ruler of a neighboring kingdom rising in alarm at the lion-incursion described in the foregoing.
Translated 'multitude.' Likely Lyc ⲁⲱⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ = ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈/ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ 'multitude, abundance' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ tentative). Modifies 'herd of lions.'

Translated 'they were gazing/looking after.' ⲙⲟⲩϩ here likely a Lyc form with sense of 'attend, watch, look toward,' possibly cognate with ⲙⲟⲩϣⲧ̄ 'examine' or contracted from it. Unusual since ⲙⲟⲩϩ normally = 'fill,' but ⲛⲉⲩⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲡⲉ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁ + object pattern fits a verb of attentive looking.

Translated 'they also leapt forth.' Construction ⲣ̄- ('do') + ⲡⲕⲉ- ('the additional/other') + ⲡⲱϩⲧ ('cast/leap') = 'they did the additional leaping/casting.' Subject 'lions' (continuing from context).

Translated 'her aspect.' ⲡⲉⲥ- 'her' + ϩⲉⲉ likely = Lyc form of ϩⲏ 'face/aspect/manner.' Subject 'she' is the cloak/garment of lions (feminine ⲧϩⲃⲥⲱ) personified as a force of wrath. The '+' marker in ⲡⲉⲥϩⲉ+ⲉ may indicate scribal correction.

Translated 'making it (a great sea)' — taking ⲉⲟⲓⲣⲁϩ as ⲉ-ⲟⲩⲉⲓⲣⲉ-ϥ (circumstantial 'while making it') and ⲟⲓⲣⲟ as related to ⲓⲟⲣⲟ 'great water/expanse' or just an intensifying repetition. The phrase qualifies the river of Tigris becoming a great sea.
Translated 'their multitude.' Possibly = ⲧⲙⲏⲣⲉ + 3pl pronoun-suffix 'their herd' (contracted), or ⲧ-ⲙⲣⲟⲩ 'the harbor'(?). Subject of ⲛⲁⲣ̄ 'shall become' in next line.
Translated as predicate of becoming-many ('how great'). Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲛⲁϣⲉ 'be many' or ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲩⲟ 'in excess.' Recurs in line 26 as ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲁⲧ 'hosts/multitudes' (translated 'hosts' there).
Translated 'uncountable.' Privative ⲛⲁⲧ- + verbal ⲱⲡ 'count' + 3sg.f. suffix -ⲥ̄. Standard Coptic privative idiom 'without counting it' = countless.

Translated 'while desiring to crush.' ⲉⲩ-ⲟⲩⲁⲱⲥ̄ = circumstantial + ⲟⲩⲱϣ-ⲥ̄ 'wanting it.' ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲉⲱⲥ = ⲁ-ⲧⲣⲉⲩ-ⲱⲱⲥ 'to make them crush' (= ⲱⲱⲥ 'beat, crush'). The archons want to crush hosts of light-beings.

Translated 'primordial-ones.' Lexeme uncertain — possibly a Lyc collective for 'first/foremost ones' or 'shadows' (ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ?), or 'molders/fashioners.' Modified by ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲏ 'of the beginning,' supporting a primordial-being reading.
Translated 'lurked and swallowed.' ⲥⲱϩⲡ̄ = 'lie in wait, lurk, ambush' (= Sah. ⲥⲱⲣⲡ̄/ⲥⲱⲣϩ̄?); ⲱⲙⲕ̄ 'swallow.' The narrative inversion: archons consume the lions (the cloak they were given to wear).
Translated 'bearers' tentatively. Possibly compound on ⲱⲗ 'carry, lift' + ⲁⲗⲱⲓⲣⲉ (unidentified). With ⲙⲡⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'of destruction' suggests instrumental agents of destruction. Confidence low.
